close_reason: Landed. Username and AccountName typed PII wrappers replace Session.username and AccountInfo.name (was String). Both have redacting Display (renders '[REDACTED]') and Debug (renders 'Username("[REDACTED]")'). expose_unredacted() returns the raw &str; the explicit accessor name surfaces caller intent. Transparent serde preserves wire round-trip. Two new canary tests in tests/log_redaction.rs exercise both %-Display and ?-Debug paths against the Username and AccountName types; the canary literal must not appear and '[REDACTED]' must.
description:
Followup to bd:JMAP-6r7c.35. Session.username and AccountInfo.name are pub String fields containing PII (typically email addresses). Debug redaction is in place but Display, Serialize, and tracing %-formatter paths still leak the raw value.

bd:JMAP-6r7c.35 added doc-warnings on both fields enumerating the leak paths. The followup recommendation is to introduce typed wrappers:

  pub struct Username(String);
  pub struct AccountName(String);

…each with:
- A manual Display impl that redacts to '<user>@…' or similar pattern.
- An explicit .expose_unredacted() -> &str method for callers who genuinely need the raw value (audit logging, etc.) so the call site documents the intent.
- A Serialize impl that emits the raw value (since the wire format requires it).
- Debug-redaction canary tests (workspace AGENTS.md Security testing Pattern 1).

This is a public-API break — every caller currently writing session.username.clone() or session.username.as_str() has to migrate. The right place to land it is the next API-break cycle (e.g. alongside JMAP-6by7 typed-Id).

Affects: crate-jmap-base-client/src/request.rs (Session, AccountInfo).
Tests: tests/log_redaction.rs (extend the existing canary harness).
title: Username/AccountName newtypes with redacting Display impl
